# Pineapple juice

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="pineapple-juice-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="pineapple-juice-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="pineapple-juice-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Pineapple juice in the HMI library has 862 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Cu, Fe, Mn and Zn from 15 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury and nickel and others, in 862 results from 15 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anastácio M, Marreilha dos Santos AP, Aschner M, Mateus L · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Determination of trace metals in fruit juices in the Portuguese market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 434-439</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the pineapple juice came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-pineapple-juice" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-pineapple-juice-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of pineapple juice, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Every source record that names pineapple juice was decided on its content: 15 occurrence extracted, 15 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Pineapple juice FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pineapple-juice" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pineapple-juice" data-question="What heavy metals are found in pineapple juice?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in pineapple juice?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Cu, Fe, Mn and Zn in pineapple juice, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anastácio M, Marreilha dos Santos AP, Aschner M, Mateus L · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Determination of trace metals in fruit juices in the Portuguese market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 434-439</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in pineapple juice, juice from 35 results in 5 reporting regions, with a subgroup median of 23 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-pineapple-juice-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-pineapple-juice-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of pineapple juice measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of pineapple juice measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 67 groups of pineapple juice ranged from 0.27 µg/kg (sample JAF2) to 608 µg/kg (sample OJA4); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/youssao2018-fruit-juices-syrup-benin|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alassane A. K. Youssao, Magloire A. N. Gbaguidi, Leonce Dovonon, Oriol Baltrons, Fabienne Seby, Mathilde Monperus, Mickael Saizonou, Henri H. Soclo, Olivier Donard · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/youssao2018-fruit-juices-syrup-benin">Levels of Minor and Trace Elements of Some Commercial Fruit Juices and Syrup Produced in Artisanal and Semi-Industrial Units in Benin Republic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/youssao2018-fruit-juices-syrup-benin">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 41 groups of pineapple juice ranged from 0.3 µg/kg (FY2015) to 28 µg/kg (FY2016); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Analytical Results for Lead in Juice Sampled Under the FDA&#39;s Toxic Elements in Food and Foodware, and Radionuclides in Food – Import and Domestic Compliance Program (FY2005-FY2018)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-pineapple-juice-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-pineapple-juice-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in pineapple juice is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in pineapple juice is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 2 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 3 µg/kg (mean) in pineapple juice, juice from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
